newsitem.title: USA: Florida jobless rate dips to 4.8 pct for December.
newsitem.headline: Florida jobless rate dips to 4.8 pct for December.

text.p: Florida's unemployment rate dipped to 4.8 percent in December from 5.1 percent in November and 5.4 percent a year ago, the state Department of Labor and Employment Security said Tuesday.
The December jobless rate was Florida's lowest since 1988.
The data represent 343,000 unemployed Floridians out of a civilian labor force of 7.07 million.

Services added the most jobs, 84,900, and had the second fastest growth rate over the year, 4 percent. Much of that growth was due to the conversion of employees in other industries to leased employment.

Trade gained the second largest number of new jobs over the year, 51,300, and grew at 3.2 percent, slightly faster than total nonfarm employment. Retail trade growth has shown improvment since last April and has outperformed wholesale trade since August.
Construction continued to increase, adding 6,400 jobs for a 2.1 percent growth rate, but remained far below the 1988-1989 peak.
Manufacturing jobs have declined by 1,400 jobs since last December, with all of the decline in non-durable goods.
The transportation, communications and public utilities sector grew by 11,300 jobs or 2.6 percent over the year. Finance, insurance and real estate gained 11,500 jobs for a 3 percent growth rate.
Government gained 26,400 jobs, for a 2.8 percent growth rate, since December 1996, with most of the increase in local government.
All of Florida's metropolitan statistical areas had over-the-year employment increases. Tampa-St Petesburg added the most jobs, 32,400, while Fort Lauderdale had the fastest growth rate, 4 percent.
Monroe County had the state's lowest unemployment rate in December, 2.1 percent, while Taylor County had the highest, 10.8 percent.
